profile.reading:
This facility at 11200 Lakeview Avenue in Lenexa, Kansas, generically named Data Center Lenexa on the map, is part of what its operator, DataBank, calls the South Lake Campus, anchored by a data center building known internally as MCI3. Lenexa sits in Johnson County, Kansas, within the greater Kansas City metropolitan area, a market that has grown into a genuine, if secondary, national hub for data center investment thanks to its central location, comparatively low exposure to hurricanes and coastal natural disasters, and available land close to major interstate highways.

DataBank's own materials describe the South Lake Campus as roughly nine acres, with the MCI3 building itself providing close to 70,000 square feet of technical space and a critical IT power capacity of about 12.75 megawatts, a substantial amount of dedicated electrical capacity reserved for customer server equipment rather than general building use. The campus sits near Interstates 35 and 435, giving it convenient access for the technicians, network engineers, and equipment deliveries that a working data center depends on daily, and DataBank markets the location's proximity to major supply chain and logistics operators, citing companies like Amazon and UPS that have a significant regional presence in the area.

Kansas City area data centers like this one function as regional colocation hubs, housing servers and networking equipment for businesses that would rather rent secure, professionally managed space with guaranteed power and cooling than build and operate their own facility. DataBank reports that the South Lake Campus hosts around fifteen onsite network carriers, giving tenants a choice of internet and connectivity providers without having to arrange their own fiber builds, and the company has described ongoing expansion of the MCI3 building to add tens of thousands of additional square feet of colocation space, a sign of continued demand in the Kansas City market. Together, the acreage, the power capacity, and the carrier density point to a real, actively operated, and still growing data center rather than a facility that exists only as a name on a map.

DataBank itself is one of the larger privately held colocation and cloud infrastructure providers in the United States, operating dozens of data centers across multiple metro markets, and the South Lake Campus fits a familiar pattern in the industry of locating suburban data center capacity near, rather than inside, a dense downtown core, trading some proximity to a city center for cheaper land, more room to expand, and easier access to redundant utility power feeds. For enterprise customers in the Kansas City region who need guaranteed uptime for financial systems, healthcare records, retail platforms, or logistics software, a facility like this one offers an alternative to running that same equipment out of an office server closet with none of the generator backup, fire suppression, or professional monitoring that a purpose built data center provides as a matter of course.
profile.research_note: Data Center Lenexa, 11200 Lakeview Ave, Lenexa KS. Confirmed via databank.com/data-centers/kansas-city/south-lake-campus as DataBank's South Lake Campus / MCI3 facility: 9 acre campus, ~66,920-69,762 sqft IT space, 12.75-12.8MW critical IT power, 15 onsite carriers, expansion in progress as of July 2024. Genuine, substantial, actively operated data center.

reading.body:
This facility has been mapped at a location in Lenexa, Kansas, but the operator is not published. Research to identify the operator has been exhausted with available tools, leaving the facility's purpose and scale unknown from public sources.

Kansas has three mapped data center facilities according to OpenStreetMap, of which none publish power consumption figures. This facility is therefore ranked first by published capacity in the state only because no other Kansas facility publishes specifications, a ranking that carries no information about its actual scale relative to peers.

Without published power, cooling, or IT specifications, this campus cannot be evaluated for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. To determine whether it matters to the grid constraints on AI deployment, future research would need to identify the operator and access their technical specifications.
